name: VitaCore ClearVeil Dermal Renewal System
body_location: subdermal facial and/or full-body dermal layer
description:
ClearVeil is a semi-biological implant system consisting of a network of micro-capillary regulators and keratinocyte stimulation nodes distributed throughout the dermal and subdermal layers, most commonly in the face and neck. The system continuously monitors local skin cell turnover, sebum production, melanin clustering, and microvascular irregularities, making real-time adjustments to keep the skin surface within user-defined parameters. It suppresses acne formation at the follicular level, prevents hyperpigmentation, regulates redness and rosacea responses, and accelerates the healing of minor surface damage such as cuts and blemishes. More advanced configurations include wrinkle-tension management, which applies micro-stimulation to underlying musculature and collagen networks to prevent and gradually reverse the formation of expression lines. The system is powered by the body's own circulatory pressure and requires no external energy source.

ClearVeil is the cosmetic dermatology appointment made permanent — the product that effectively ended the market for topical skincare in its traditional form. VitaCore markets it primarily to adults in their late twenties and older, though a significant percentage of teenage users install the acne-suppression configuration as soon as they can afford it or convince a parent to co-sign the clinic visit. For people on the Shelf, ClearVeil often represents a meaningful quality-of-life investment — skin problems that would have required expensive dermatology visits are simply no longer an issue. In corporate tiers, 'clean skin' is so thoroughly normalized via ClearVeil that those who cannot afford it are quietly marked by its absence. The implant has largely replaced the concept of a skincare routine, freeing up time and money that users previously spent on products.
installation_requirements: Outpatient clinic; facial configuration takes approximately 90 minutes under local anesthetic; full-body installations require a half-day procedure
maintenance: Annual calibration visit to adjust skin parameters as user ages or preferences change; no hardware replacement typically needed for 10-year rated lifespan

side_effects: Skin may appear unusually uniform and 'flat' in texture during first month while system calibrates
Mild flushing sensation across treated areas during initial installation week
Occasional over-suppression of melanin response resulting in temporary pale patches (correctable via app)
Some users report reduced tactile sensitivity in treated facial areas, typically resolving within 6 weeks
cultural_context: ClearVeil has produced a significant and sometimes uncomfortable cultural shift around the concept of 'natural' skin. In tiers where ClearVeil saturation is high, skin that shows normal human variation — pores, minor discoloration, expression lines — is increasingly read as either a class marker (you cannot afford the implant) or a deliberate counter-cultural statement. A small movement called 'dermalism' advocates loudly for the right to visible skin, arguing that the normalization of ClearVeil creates invisible pressure on people to erase natural features. On the Shelf, where the acne-only configuration is within reach but the full renewal system is aspirational, the implant functions as a visible class aspiration — getting the full ClearVeil is a milestone, like buying a good coat. Among older Tier 4 and 5 users, the wrinkle management configuration is so thoroughly normalized that visible aging has become genuinely rare in those populations.

Working professionals who previously spent significant income on dermatology and skincare products
Older adults using the wrinkle-management configuration as a less invasive alternative to surgical procedures
People with chronic skin conditions such as rosacea or hyperpigmentation seeking permanent management
Shelf residents for whom the basic configuration represents a meaningful quality-of-life improvement

A forensic investigator realizes that a murder victim's ClearVeil implant logged every micro-injury and healing event for the past decade — the implant's data is a perfect record of abuse that someone very powerful wants buried
